entry.content:

Karthikey Hegde discovered that his internet service provider was intercepting his plaintext DNS queries and returning tampered IP addresses. By comparing standard lookups with encrypted alternatives like Cloudflare's DNS over HTTPS endpoint, he confirmed that his ISP was altering network traffic destinations.

The discovery highlighted common misconceptions surrounding tools like Unbound and DNSSEC, clarifying that while DNSSEC verifies authenticity through cryptographic signatures, it does not encrypt traffic in transit. To protect his homelab network, the author deployed AdGuard with dnscrypt-proxy to ensure all upstream queries remain encrypted.

entry.title: Steal My Bitcoin Experiment Tests PHP2Shell Exploitability
entry.content:
Links: pavursec.com | lobsters | hacker news

The PHP2Shell vulnerability was tested through the "Steal My Bitcoin" experiment to determine if it was exploitable in a live environment and if AI could assist unskilled attackers. The challenge used a PHP website hosting a $500 bitcoin wallet and a binary that outputs the wallet's private key upon successful exploitation. Although one participant successfully exploited the server, the experiment found that unskilled attackers using AI were largely unsuccessful.

The experiment attracted approximately 120,000 unique visitors and generated 13 million HTTP requests. Out of 20,000 substantive attempts, only one participant successfully exfiltrated data. These results suggest that while the vulnerability is practical to exploit, the technical complexity of the attack limits success among non-experts, despite reports of its potential for widespread exploitation.

entry.title: RAMBO Research Demonstrates Data Leakage from Air-Gapped Computers via RAM Radio Signals
entry.content:
Links: arxiv.org | hacker news

Researchers have detailed a novel cyberattack method named RAMBO that enables malware to exfiltrate sensitive data from physically isolated, air-gapped computers. By manipulating memory buses, compromised systems can generate covert radio frequency signals encoding files, cryptographic keys, and biometric information. Using off-the-shelf software-defined radio hardware and simple antennas, attackers can intercept these raw emissions from a distance and translate them back into binary data.

The technique achieves a data leakage rate of up to 1,000 bits per second, presenting significant risks for high-security environments relying on network isolation. While the method requires nearby radio equipment and custom malware implementation, it highlights hardware emission vulnerabilities that bypass traditional air-gap protections. The paper also outlines potential countermeasures to detect and mitigate out-of-band memory bus emissions.

entry.title: Pivot Database Engine Explains Impact of Memory Latency on Database Performance
entry.content:
Links: pivotlake.io | hacker news

High database CPU utilization frequently masks underlying memory stalls rather than intense computation, as modern RAM access speeds lag hundreds of instructions behind CPU processing capabilities. A naive GROUP BY implementation causes frequent cache misses that force the processor to wait on cold memory from DRAM.

To mitigate this bottleneck, the Pivot database engine implements a two-phase radix partitioning approach that breaks down large aggregation tasks into smaller pieces. By ensuring that working hash tables fit within the CPU caches, this optimization significantly reduces DRAM load operations and accelerates query execution times.

entry.title: Parameter Researchers Disclose ChatGPT Share Link Vulnerability Enabling Account Takeover
entry.content:
Links: parameter.ai | hacker news

Researchers at Parameter disclosed a security vulnerability in ChatGPT's web application that allowed a maliciously crafted public share link to execute arbitrary JavaScript within a victim's signed-in session. By combining an interactive graph feature, MathLive message handling flaws, and a Content Security Policy bypass involving YouTube, an attacker could traverse the preview sandbox and access authenticated frontend APIs. This enabled the retrieval of private conversation histories and complete account compromise simply by having a user open a shared link.

OpenAI classified the issue as a P1 bug and rolled out fixes across ChatGPT's web frontends, fully resolving the vulnerability by October 26, 2026. The vulnerability highlights the risks that emerge when multiple independent features—such as sandboxed previews, cross-frame messaging, and math layout libraries—interact unexpectedly. The incident underscores the importance of strict origin validation, secure message handling, and robust sandboxing for dynamically created documents.

entry.title: Mozilla Details Strategy to Defend Firefox Against Automated Patch-Gapping
entry.content:
Links: blog.mozilla.org | lobsters

Mozilla is adapting Firefox's security practices to counter patch-gapping, a vulnerability exploitation method accelerated by AI models that can rapidly reverse-engineer software security fixes. While frontier models have enabled the Firefox team to significantly increase its security fix rate, malicious actors are increasingly using automated tools to target the brief window of time between a code fix and full user deployment.

To neutralize this threat regardless of attack speed, Firefox is introducing a structural defense that staggers fixes across independent sandbox layers so that interdependent vulnerabilities do not share overlapping patch gaps. Additionally, the browser team is accelerating its release cycle, withholding regression tests until fixes are shipped, and scanning new code commits to maintain a security advantage over automated attackers.
